purpose: Reference cases whose Visio result depends on the reference machine rather than the drawing. Each stays visible in the comparison as 'disposed' with its reason; none counts as agreement.

cases.TEXTWIDTH-1: Visio's default style uses Calibri, which macOS does not include; MacVisio substitutes Arial. With a font both have (ARIAL-*, METRIC-*), widths agree within 0.0001 in.
cases.DOCPROPS-13: DOCLASTPRINT converts the stored UTC time to the host's time zone; the reference guest and the Mac are in different zones.
cases.MATHX-33: FONTTOID returns the index in the running Visio's installed-font table, which no drawing records.
cases.GEOM-36: RECTSECT with a negative width is degenerate; Visio's result for it is not derivable from the documented contract.
cases.ACTIONS-1: CALLTHIS runs VBA in Visio. MacVisio never executes document code (open blocker: unmodified VBA/COM/add-ins), so the formula keeps its cached value.
cases.ACTIONS-11: RUNADDON runs add-in code; see ACTIONS-1.
cases.ACTIONS-12: RUNADDONWARGS runs add-in code; see ACTIONS-1.
cases.COERCE-7: Visio holds 25.4 mm as 0.9999999999999999 in memory but saves it as 1, so the saved drawing (which MacVisio reads, and Visio itself reopens) gives BITXOR(1,1) = 0.

prefixes.FIELDCODE-date-4: East Asian calendar pictures (Japanese era, Republic of China and Korean dates) are out of scope with Japanese input (SD-2026-10-24-02); Visio 2019 itself shows the obsolete 平成 era for 2026.
prefixes.FIELDCODE-num-4: East Asian calendar pictures, as above.

open.ROUNDING-16: Open (WP-15-T02): Visio rounds geometry cells (drawing units) in internal units but explicit unit literals in their display units; MacVisio does not yet distinguish the two on metric pages.
